record.office: President Pro Tempore, Connecticut State Senate
record.t: Announced he will not seek reelection to the Connecticut State Senate in 2026.
record.q: announced today that he will not seek reelection to the Connecticut State Senate in 2026, concluding a 46-year legislative career that began in 1981.

record.t: Was elected by the members of the Connecticut State Senate to serve as President Pro Tempore (2015).
record.q: In January of 2015, Senator Looney was elected by the members of the State Senate to serve as President Pro Tempore, the highest-ranking legislator in the Connecticut General Assembly.

record.t: Was elected to the Connecticut State Senate in 1992, after six terms as a State Representative.
record.q: having been elected to the State Senate in 1992, following six terms as a State Representative.

record.t: Was appointed an Assistant Majority Leader and served as House Chair of the Planning and Development Committee, the Government Administration and Elections Committee, and the Appropriations Judicial Subcommittee.
record.q: Senator Looney was appointed an Assistant Majority Leader and served as House Chair of the Planning and Development Committee, the Government Administration and Elections Committee, and the Appropriations Judicial Subcommittee

record.t: Was re-elected President Pro Tempore of the State Senate in 2017, 2019, 2021, 2023 and 2025.
record.q: He was re-elected to that position in January of 2017, January 2019, January 2021, January 2023, and again in January 2025.

record.t: Served 12 years as Senate Majority Leader before becoming Senate President.
record.q: Prior to his election as Senate President, Senator Looney served 12 years as Senate Majority Leader.

record.t: Served three terms as Senate Chair of the Finance, Revenue and Bonding Committee, one term as Senate Chair of the Banks Committee, and one term as Senate Ranking Member of the Judiciary Committee.
record.q: he served three terms as Senate Chair of the Finance, Revenue and Bonding Committee; one term as Senate Chair of the Banks Committee; and one term as the Senate Ranking Member of the Judiciary Committee.
